security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks in documentation examples, resource URLs, and example identifiers. I found no prompt-injection language or automatic execution path in SKILL.md. The remaining concern is setup guidance that asks users to run unpinned npx commands against a third-party service.

remediation.suggestion: Pin flow-nexus to a reviewed version and include package verification guidance before asking users to run MCP setup, registration, or login commands.

remediation.issue: External service authentication and data handling
remediation.suggestion: State what data is sent to Flow Nexus during training, prediction, registration, and login, and link to privacy and security documentation.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned External Package Execution in Setup Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The setup section instructs users to run npx flow-nexus@latest for MCP setup, registration, and login. Using the mutable latest tag executes package code from the network without pinned version or integrity guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 23-29 clearly show npx commands using @latest. This requires user action rather than automatic execution, so the risk is material but not critical.

content.user_title: Train Neural Models with Flow Nexus
content.value_statement: Neural model workflows are hard to configure across sandboxes and teams. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidance for Flow Nexus training, inference, clusters, and templates.
actual_capabilities: Configure feedforward, LSTM, GAN, autoencoder, and transformer training jobs.
Plan model inference requests for trained Flow Nexus models.
Browse, deploy, rate, and publish marketplace neural templates.
Create distributed training clusters with worker and aggregator nodes.
Monitor training jobs, cluster status, and benchmark results.
Prepare federated learning workflows where supported by Flow Nexus.
limitations: Requires Flow Nexus authentication and MCP server setup.
Does not include local training code or model weights.
Examples assume valid dataset, model, cluster, and user identifiers.
Costs, limits, and privacy controls depend on the Flow Nexus service.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Neural Classifier
use_cases.description: Plan a small training job, choose an architecture, and monitor progress before larger experiments.

use_cases.title: Operate Distributed Training
use_cases.description: Create Flow Nexus clusters, deploy worker nodes, and track training health across sandboxes.

use_cases.title: Reuse Marketplace Models
use_cases.description: Find a template, deploy it with custom settings, run predictions, and benchmark performance.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Training Job
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a supervised model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-nexus-neural to plan a small training job for [task]. Recommend the architecture, tier, epochs, batch size, learning rate, and monitoring steps.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a Template Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-nexus-neural to find a marketplace template for [domain]. Explain how to deploy it, customize training settings, run predictions, and benchmark results.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Distributed Cluster
prompt_templates.scenario: Scale training across multiple E2B sandboxes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-nexus-neural to design a distributed training cluster for [model goal]. Include topology, node roles, training settings, monitoring checks, and shutdown steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Federated Learning
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-nexus-neural to plan a federated learning workflow for [sensitive dataset]. Include cluster setup, aggregation rounds, validation, privacy assumptions, and operational risks.

output_examples.input: Train a small classifier for customer support labels.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes a feedforward architecture, small resource tier, training settings, validation checks, and monitoring steps.

output_examples.input: Deploy a sentiment template and compare inference latency.
output: A suitable sentiment template is selected from the marketplace.
Deployment settings are described in plain language.
The benchmark plan compares latency, throughput, and accuracy.

output_examples.input: Set up federated training for regional medical datasets.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines cluster topology, worker roles, aggregation settings, privacy assumptions, and validation requirements.

best_practices: Start with nano or mini tiers, then scale only after validation.
Pin setup package versions and verify the Flow Nexus service before running commands.
Track model, job, cluster, and template identifiers for every workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not run mutable latest setup commands in restricted environments without review.
Do not train on sensitive data without approved privacy and retention controls.
Do not publish templates before benchmarking and validation are complete.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps an AI assistant plan Flow Nexus neural training, inference, distributed clusters, templates, and model management tasks.

faq.question: Does it train models locally?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflows use Flow Nexus MCP tools and distributed E2B sandbox environments.

faq.question: Do I need a Flow Nexus account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill states that distributed training requires authentication and Flow Nexus MCP setup.

faq.question: Which architectures are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers feedforward networks, LSTMs, GANs, autoencoders, and transformers.

faq.question: Can it support federated learning?
faq.answer: Yes, where Flow Nexus supports the required cluster, node, and aggregation settings.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review the external npx setup commands, service authentication, data handling requirements, and Flow Nexus costs.
